entry_conditions: Use after closed-grasp retrieval or at an intermediate shared state when two causal frames provide TCP/peg motion and peg-to-hole geometry. It does not require nominal index-1120 timing, but support contains only successful-path states.
exit_conditions: Hand off when peg/hole relations show near-axis alignment, y/z centering and descent toward insertion height, using the shared [1380,1500) interval for a multi-chunk transition.
overlap_role: All [1120,1500) actions remain supervised: 7.5 seconds [1120,1270) overlap retrieval and 6.0 seconds [1380,1500) overlap alignment/insertion. The TCP frame is reanchored only after each 8 executed actions.
successor_readiness: align_and_insert_peg is ready when the peg remains held, is aligned and centered, and is at or descending toward hole height. If the hole itself moved, prefer the destination-frame policy.
failure_signatures: Local chunks oscillate or stop reducing geometric error, peg/TCP coupling is lost, clearance falls near the box, accumulated anchor error grows, a large scene shift needs a different global route, or IK is unconverged/at limits.
continuation_guidance: Preserve both causal frames across switches, recompute the TCP anchor at every replan, execute only slots 1-8, and never advance phase state during denoising. Monitor coupling and solver diagnostics before continuing.
limitations: This is not unseen-error recovery. It cannot repair a dropped peg, collision or bad grasp. TCP-relative labels improve local conditioning but are not by themselves invariant to a moved destination, and fixed anchors may accumulate model/execution error within a chunk.
